result: ARID1A is expressed during pachytene spermatogenesis and becomes enriched on sex chromosomes during diplonema. Arid1a mRNA is expressed at pachynema, while Arid1b is undetectable until late spermiogenesis. ARID1A protein is uniformly distributed in pachytene but preferentially enriched on sex chromosomes in late diplonema.
evaluation: Reviewers describe the data as 'convincing' and 'solid,' noting that ARID1A accumulates at the XY body late in Prophase I. The expression patterns and localization data are accepted without challenge.

result: Loss of ARID1A causes pachytene arrest with accumulation of mutant spermatocytes at mid-pachynema and failure to progress to diplotene or metaphase-I. ARID1A-deficient cells fail to repress sex-linked genes, indicating defective MSCI.
evaluation: Reviewers state 'the data demonstrate that the mutant cells fail to progress past pachytene' and describe the phenotypes as 'clear and specific.' One reviewer notes 'it is unclear whether this specifically reflects pachytene arrest' versus accumulation in other prophase stages, but the overall arrest phenotype is accepted.

result: The Stra8-Cre system produces incomplete recombination with ~70-74% of pachytene spermatocytes lacking ARID1A, while 'escaper' cells retain ARID1A and progress through meiosis normally, producing mature spermatozoa.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge 'the conditional KO mouse model has some inherent limitations due to incomplete recombination and the existence of 'escaper' cells' but state 'the authors have addressed this point thoroughly and have demonstrated clear and specific phenotypes using the best available animal model.'

result: RNA-seq reveals that 53% of sex-linked genes are misexpressed in ARID1A-deficient pachytene spermatocytes, with 86.4% showing elevated expression. Sex chromosome expression is significantly higher than autosomal expression, implicating ARID1A in MSCI.
evaluation: Reviewers note that 'by RNAseq [the authors] observe significant misexpression of sex-linked genes that typically are silenced at pachytene' and describe this as part of the 'convincing' data supporting MSCI defects.

result: CUT&RUN shows ARID1A occupancy at promoters of differentially regulated genes, with preferential association at promoters of normally repressed sex-linked genes during pachynema.
evaluation: This finding is presented as supporting evidence for ARID1A's role in MSCI and is not challenged by reviewers. It is part of the overall 'solid data' that reviewers accept.

result: DDR signaling factors (γH2Ax, ATR, MDC1) localize normally to the sex body in ARID1A-deficient cells, indicating that sex-linked DDR signaling occurs independently of ARID1A.
evaluation: Reviewers state 'the revised manuscript more appropriately describes the relationship between ARID1A and DNA damage response (DDR) signaling' and note 'the authors don't see defects in a few DDR markers in ARID1A CKO cells...suggesting that ARID1A may not be required for meiotic DDR signaling.' The assessment of ATR is noted as 'low resolution' but the overall conclusion is accepted.

result: ARID1A-deficient sex chromosomes display abnormal presence of elongating RNA polymerase II (pSer2-RNAPII), with a 1.5-fold increase in RNAPII fluorescence on sex chromosomes. ARID1A facilitates sex-linked gene repression by limiting elongating RNAPII association.
evaluation: Reviewers note the authors 'show that ARID1A is required for exclusion of RNA PolII from the sex body' as part of the MSCI defect phenotype. This is accepted as part of the 'convincing' data.

result: ATAC-seq reveals increased chromatin accessibility in ARID1A-deficient cells, with a dramatic shift toward promoter-associated peaks. Sex-linked genes show greater accessibility at TSSs, particularly for up-regulated genes, suggesting BAF complexes limit promoter accessibility on sex chromosomes.
evaluation: Reviewers state the authors 'show that ARID1A is required for...limiting promoter accessibility at sex-linked genes, consistent with a meiotic sex chromosome inactivation (MSCI) defect.' This is part of the accepted dataset.

result: ARID1A promotes preferential enrichment of H3.3 on sex chromosomes during pachynema. Without ARID1A, sex chromosomes are depleted of H3.3 at levels resembling autosomes, with 89% of mid and 77% of late pachytene spermatocytes lacking typical H3.3 sex body enrichment.
evaluation: Reviewers note 'upon loss of ARID1A, overall H3.3 enrichment at the sex body as measured by IF failed to occur' and describe this as part of the study's 'new insights into the process of MSCI from the perspective of chromatin composition and structure.'

result: CUT&RUN reveals shifts in H3.3 localization from intergenic sites and gene-body domains to promoters in ARID1A-deficient cells. H3.3 peaks shift from predominantly sex-linked intergenic (98%) to autosomal genic regions (94.5%), with striking TSS accumulation on sex-linked genes.
evaluation: Reviewers note 'H3.3 was enriched specifically at transcription start sites of sex-linked genes that are normally regulated by ARID1A' and state 'the results suggest that ARID1A normally prevents H3.3 accumulation at target promoters on sex chromosomes and...restricts H3.3 to intergenic sites.'

result: Loss of ARID1A causes abnormal retention of canonical histones H3.1/3.2 on sex chromosomes, with increased proportions of mid (66%) and late (40%) pachytene spermatocytes retaining H3.1/3.2 on sex-linked chromatin.
evaluation: This finding is part of the chromatin composition changes that reviewers accept as demonstrating ARID1A's role in MSCI. It is not specifically challenged.

result: H3.3 chaperones DAXX and HIRA show unchanged levels and localization in ARID1A-deficient cells, and total H3.3 protein levels are unchanged, indicating ARID1A impacts H3.3 localization without affecting its expression.
evaluation: These control experiments support the interpretation that ARID1A affects H3.3 distribution rather than expression. Reviewers do not challenge these findings.

result: Autosomal genes show H3.3 enrichment at TSSs that is enhanced in ARID1A-deficient cells. Both sex-linked and autosomal targets display concordant increases in H3.3 TSS occupancy, with ARID1A preventing H3.3 accumulation at target promoters.
evaluation: This is part of the genome-wide H3.3 redistribution pattern that reviewers accept as demonstrating ARID1A's regulatory role.

result: Integration of ATAC-seq and H3.3 CUT&RUN reveals that accessible chromatin regions show either loss or gain of H3.3 occupancy. Sites losing H3.3 are intergenic, while sites gaining H3.3 are genic, supporting that ARID1A restricts H3.3 to intergenic sites and prevents redistribution to genic regions.
evaluation: This integrated analysis is part of the 'valuable dataset' that reviewers accept. The interpretation about H3.3 redistribution is consistent with reviewer summaries.

result: Gained ATAC-seq peaks show enrichment of PRDM9 motifs and DMC1/H3K4me3 occupancy at regions normally devoid of H3.3, suggesting antagonism between H3.3 occupancy and meiotic DSB sites. ARID1A may indirectly influence DNA DSB repair by regulating H3.3 localization.
evaluation: Reviewers note the study 'present[s] data implicating ARID1A and H3.3 occupancy in DSB repair' and describe this as raising 'interesting new questions about the interplay between chromatin structure, meiotic silencing and DNA repair.'

result: ARID1A is required for normal DMC1 localization to sex chromosomes. ARID1A-deficient cells show marked reduction in DMC1 foci on sex chromosomes, and sex-linked intergenic sites with ARID1A-dependent H3.3 enrichment are depleted for DMC1. Loss of ARID1A causes H3.3 redistribution to regions normally associated with DMC1.
evaluation: Reviewers note 'the authors present data implicating ARID1A and H3.3 occupancy in DSB repair, finding that ARID1A cKO leads to a reduction in focus formation by DMC1, a key repair protein' and describe the observation of 'reduced sex chromosome association by DMC1' as 'interesting.'

result: RAD51 localization to sex chromosomes is unaffected by ARID1A loss, with normal RAD51 foci formation along asynapsed axes. ARID1A is necessary for DMC1 but not RAD51 sex-linked association.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state 'only a single image of RAD51 staining in the cKO is provided (Fig. S11) and there are no associated quantitative data provided. The data are suggestive and conclusions about the impacts of ARID1A loss on RAD51 must be considered as preliminary until more rigorously assessed.'

result: ARID1A-directed H3.3 localization influences both meiotic sex chromosome gene regulation and DNA repair. BAF-A promotes H3.3 accumulation on sex chromosomes at mid-pachynema, coinciding with H3.1/3.2 eviction and RNAPII exclusion. ARID1A has a dual role in regulating sex chromosome repression and DNA repair, promoting meiotic progression.
evaluation: Reviewers summarize that 'the paper provides new insights into the process of MSCI from the perspective of chromatin composition and structure and raises interesting new questions about the interplay between chromatin structure, meiotic silencing and DNA repair.' They describe this as a 'valuable dataset' with 'solid data' that 'generally support the conclusions.'
